title: Lior and the Cover
premise: Freya Zhou, a peace-delegation interpreter with a packed go-bag and a fabricated past, receives a meeting invitation from their handler — sent hours after the handler's death. Following it, they discover the 'peace talks' are cover for an arms-for-hostages deal that three governments will burn the delegation to protect. Hunted by an assassin who was once the handler's protégé, Freya must smuggle the truth to a journalist, a defector, and the one delegation member they trust. The extraction flight at dawn becomes the deadline: Freya chooses truth over loyalty, exposes the deal mid-flight over international waters, and survives by trading their polished lie for a real name.
about_author: Ansel Voss is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade in rooms where nothing said meant what it sounded like. They write thrillers about people whose job is to be invisible, and they have never once confirmed which delegations they served.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. During a stalled negotiation in Geneva, Freya's handler Ilse is found dead in her hotel room — ruled a heart attack. That night, Freya's encrypted work channel pings: a meeting invitation from Ilse, timestamped for tomorrow, 4 a.m., location attached. Freya packs the go-bag out of habit and goes. Emotional beat: dread sharpened into compulsion; the first crack in the lie Freya calls a life.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Alternating Freya and assassin Tomas's POV. At the 4 a.m. site — a decommissioned airfield hangar — Freya finds Ilse's hidden dossier proving the talks mask an arms-for-hostages swap sanctioned across three governments. Tomas, sent to retrieve and destroy it, recognizes Freya as the interpreter Ilse trusted most and hesitates. Freya escapes with copies but loses their passport. Emotional beat: vertigo of realizing every ally is compromised.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, intercut with delegation radio traffic. With dawn extraction looming, Freya runs a relay: a burned journalist, a defecting analyst, and delegate Amara Okafor — the one person whose loyalty isn't for sale. Each handoff costs something; Tomas closes in, wounded by his own orders. In a tram tunnel, he corners Freya and instead asks what Ilse promised them both. Emotional beat: found family forged under fire; loyalty and truth stop being opposites.

chapters.title: Wheels Up
chapters.summary: Full-cast POV convergence. Freya boards the extraction flight carrying the dossier and Tomas, now a witness, carrying his confession. Mid-flight over open water, Freya broadcasts the truth on the delegation's own channel, forcing the three governments to choose between shooting down their own plane or absorbing the scandal. They land; the story breaks; the cover collapses. Freya surrenders the false identity and gives Amara their real name. Emotional beat: costly, quiet triumph — inheritance claimed, not received.
